examples.question: Is C-reactive protein stable in serum gel tubes exposed to delayed centrifugation and variable temperatures?
gold_answers: C-reactive protein appears stable under the serum gel tube conditions tested by Tanner et al. The study listed CRP among analytes remaining stable when samples were stored at 15, 25, or 35 °C for 4, 8, or 24 hours before centrifugation.

gold_documents.title: Stability of common biochemical analytes in serum gel tubes subjected to various storage temperatures and times pre-centrifugation
gold_documents.author: Tanner M, et al.

examples.question: Is vitamin D stable in serum gel tubes before centrifugation under field-like temperature delays?
gold_answers: Vitamin D appears stable under the delayed pre-centrifugation serum gel tube conditions tested by Tanner et al. Vitamin D was included among analytes reported stable at 15, 25, or 35 °C for 4, 8, or 24 hours before centrifugation.

gold_documents.title: Stability of common biochemical analytes in serum gel tubes subjected to various storage temperatures and times pre-centrifugation
gold_documents.author: Tanner M, et al.

examples.question: Can short-term processing delays up to 15 hours affect serum and plasma cytokine measurements?
gold_answers: Short-term processing delays can affect cytokine measurements, but the overall changes were generally small in the Gottfried-Blackmore et al. study. They observed short-term delays produced changes in serum and plasma cytokines within roughly −10.8% to 43.5%, with some analyte-specific exceptions.

gold_documents.title: Effects of processing conditions on stability of immune analytes in human blood
gold_documents.author: Gottfried-Blackmore A, et al.

examples.question: Can serum and plasma be used interchangeably for cytokine or proteomic analyses after processing delay?
gold_answers: Serum and plasma should not be used interchangeably for cytokine or proteomic analyses. Gottfried-Blackmore et al. reported poor correlation between serum and plasma cytokines and concluded that cytokine studies should consider the non-equivalence between serum and plasma.

gold_documents.title: Effects of processing conditions on stability of immune analytes in human blood
gold_documents.author: Gottfried-Blackmore A, et al.

examples.question: Is whole blood gene expression largely stable during short-term processing delays up to 15 hours?
gold_answers: Whole blood gene expression was largely stable under the short-term processing delay conditions tested by Gottfried-Blackmore et al. They reported that pooled gene expression levels did not show significant effects across their short-term room temperature and 4 °C delay conditions.

gold_documents.title: Effects of processing conditions on stability of immune analytes in human blood
gold_documents.author: Gottfried-Blackmore A, et al.

examples.question: Should flow or mass cytometry studies avoid processing delays greater than 5 hours for susceptible PBMC populations?
gold_answers: Yes. Gottfried-Blackmore et al. concluded that flow and mass cytometry studies should avoid delays greater than 5 hours when studying susceptible cell populations. They observed significant cellular changes especially at 15 hours at 4 °C, including effects on live singlets, monocytes, Treg, and CD8+ T cells.

gold_documents.title: Effects of processing conditions on stability of immune analytes in human blood
gold_documents.author: Gottfried-Blackmore A, et al.

examples.question: Do processing delays up to 72 hours at room temperature or 4 degrees Celsius significantly affect plasma cytokines?
gold_answers: In the Gyorffy et al. study, delayed processing up to 72 hours at room temperature or 4 °C did not significantly affect plasma cytokines in samples from healthy volunteers and ICU patients. This supports a simplified biosampling protocol for the measured plasma markers, although the conclusion is source- and assay-specific.

gold_documents.title: Impact of sample processing delays on plasma markers of inflammation, chemotaxis, cell death, and blood coagulation
gold_documents.author: Gyorffy VJ, et al.

examples.question: Are plasma chemokines stable after delayed processing up to 72 hours at room temperature or 4 degrees Celsius?
gold_answers: In the Gyorffy et al. study, plasma chemokines were not significantly affected by delayed processing up to 72 hours at either room temperature or 4 °C. This applies to their measured chemokines and study design.

gold_documents.title: Impact of sample processing delays on plasma markers of inflammation, chemotaxis, cell death, and blood coagulation
gold_documents.author: Gyorffy VJ, et al.

examples.question: Is plasma cell-free DNA affected by sample processing delays up to 72 hours at room temperature or 4 degrees Celsius?
gold_answers: In the Gyorffy et al. study, plasma cfDNA was not significantly affected by delayed processing up to 72 hours at room temperature or 4 °C. The study measured cfDNA using Picogreen DNA quantification.

gold_documents.title: Impact of sample processing delays on plasma markers of inflammation, chemotaxis, cell death, and blood coagulation
gold_documents.author: Gyorffy VJ, et al.

examples.question: Does delayed processing up to 72 hours affect plasma blood clotting potential measured by thrombin generation?
gold_answers: In the Gyorffy et al. study, delayed processing up to 72 hours at room temperature or 4 °C did not significantly affect thrombin formation or blood clotting potential in plasma samples.

gold_documents.title: Impact of sample processing delays on plasma markers of inflammation, chemotaxis, cell death, and blood coagulation
gold_documents.author: Gyorffy VJ, et al.

examples.question: Does long-term storage at minus 20 degrees Celsius versus minus 80 degrees Celsius affect serum metabolomic and proteomic biomarkers?
gold_answers: Yes. Valo et al. found that storage at −20 °C versus −80 °C can affect serum metabolomic and proteomic biomarkers. After quality control, 193 analytes were evaluated; 120 were apparently unaffected, but 15 were clearly susceptible to −20 °C versus −80 °C storage.

gold_documents.title: Effect of serum sample storage temperature on metabolomic and proteomic biomarkers
gold_documents.author: Valo E, et al.

examples.question: Is glutamine susceptible to long-term serum storage at minus 20 degrees Celsius compared with minus 80 degrees Celsius?
gold_answers: Yes. Valo et al. identified glutamine among analytes affected by −20 °C versus −80 °C storage and also reported that storage time was associated with changes involving glutamine and the glutamate/glutamine ratio.

gold_documents.title: Effect of serum sample storage temperature on metabolomic and proteomic biomarkers
gold_documents.author: Valo E, et al.

examples.question: Can serum glutamate/glutamine ratio indicate sub-optimal long-term storage at minus 20 degrees Celsius?
gold_answers: Yes. Valo et al. identified serum glutamate/glutamine ratio greater than 0.20 as a sensitive and specific indicator of storage at −20 °C compared with −80 °C in their type 1 diabetes serum sample datasets.

gold_documents.title: Effect of serum sample storage temperature on metabolomic and proteomic biomarkers
gold_documents.author: Valo E, et al.

examples.question: Do plasma and serum metabolomic profiles depend on pre-analytical factors such as processing delay and freeze-thaw cycles?
gold_answers: Yes. Stevens et al. reviewed pre-analytical factors in metabolomic studies and concluded that plasma and serum metabolomic profiles are affected by factors including fasting status, hemolysis, collection time, processing delays, especially at room temperature, and repeated freeze-thaw cycles.

gold_documents.title: Pre-Analytical Factors that Affect Metabolite Stability in Human Urine, Plasma, and Serum: A Review
gold_documents.author: Stevens VL, et al.

examples.question: Can multiple freeze-thaw cycles alter urine metabolomic findings?
gold_answers: Yes. Stevens et al. reported that urine metabolomic findings can be altered by several pre-analytical factors, including collection time, fasting, centrifugation conditions, filtration/additives, normalization procedures, and multiple freeze-thaw cycles.

gold_documents.title: Pre-Analytical Factors that Affect Metabolite Stability in Human Urine, Plasma, and Serum: A Review
gold_documents.author: Stevens VL, et al.

examples.question: Does one freeze-thaw cycle after storage at minus 70 degrees Celsius meaningfully affect common nutritional, NCD, and inflammatory biomarkers in serum?
gold_answers: In the Abraham et al. study, a single freeze-thaw cycle after one month of storage at −70 °C had minimal effect on the studied nutritional, noncommunicable disease, and inflammatory biomarkers. Some analytes differed statistically from baseline, but all changes were within acceptable total allowable error limits.

gold_documents.title: The Effects of a Single Freeze-Thaw Cycle on Concentrations of Nutritional, Noncommunicable Disease, and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Serum Samples
gold_documents.author: Abraham RA, et al.

examples.question: Which biochemical analytes were not stable in serum gel tubes after delayed pre-centrifugation storage?
gold_answers: Potassium, glucose, phosphate, creatinine, urea, ferritin, iron, lactate dehydrogenase, magnesium and calcium were not stable in at least one of the storage conditions.

gold_documents.title: Stability of common biochemical analytes in serum gel tubes subjected to various storage temperatures and times pre-centrifugation
gold_documents.author: Tanner et al.

examples.question: Which analytes became unstable after 4 hours of delayed centrifugation in serum gel tube samples stored at room temperature?
gold_answers: Calcium, gamma-glutamyl transferase, glucose, inorganic phosphate and potassium were found to be unstable in serum after 4 h of delayed centrifugation.

gold_documents.title: Impact of delayed centrifugation on the stability of 32 biochemical analytes in blood samples collected in serum gel tubes and stored at room temperature
gold_documents.author: Sanz-Felisi et al.

examples.question: Which routine biochemical analytes were exceptions to stability after delayed blood separation up to 12 hours?
gold_answers: The majority of analytes were stable with delayed separation up to 12 h, except for potassium, C-peptide, osteocalcin, parathyroid hormone (PTH), bicarbonate and LDH.

gold_documents.title: Stability of routine biochemical analytes in whole blood and plasma/serum: focus on potassium stability from lithium heparin
gold_documents.author: Dupuy et al.

examples.question: How stable were most of the 81 analytes before centrifugation under the tested storage conditions?
gold_answers: Most of the analytes investigated remained stable up to 24 h under all storage conditions prior to centrifugation.

gold_documents.title: Stability study of 81 analytes in human whole blood, in serum and in plasma
gold_documents.author: Oddoze et al.

examples.question: Which biochemistry analytes were significantly impacted by delayed centrifugation across plasma, serum and whole blood?
gold_answers: Glucose, potassium, and aspartate aminotransferase, among others, were significantly impacted by delayed centrifugation, having been found to be unstable in whole blood specimens.

gold_documents.title: The stability of 65 biochemistry analytes in plasma, serum, and whole blood
gold_documents.author: Zhou et al.

examples.question: Did different pre-analytical handling procedures change blood and urine metabolomic profiles?
gold_answers: Appropriate procedures for blood derivatives collection and urine preservation/storage that allow maintaining as much as possible the original metabolic profile of the fresh samples emerge.

gold_documents.title: Standard operating procedures for pre-analytical handling of blood and urine for metabolomic studies and biobanks
gold_documents.author: Bernini et al.

examples.question: What proportion of quantified urine metabolites remained stable across the tested storage conditions?
gold_answers: Our findings indicate that 78% of quantified metabolites were stable for all examined storage conditions.

gold_documents.title: Stability of targeted metabolite profiles of urine samples under different storage conditions
gold_documents.author: Rotter et al.

examples.question: Which pre-analytical factors affected metabolomic profiles in plasma and serum samples?
gold_answers: For plasma and serum samples, metabolomic profiles were affected by fasting status, hemolysis, collection time, processing delays, particularly at room temperature, and repeated freeze/thaw cycles.

gold_documents.title: Pre-Analytical Factors that Affect Metabolite Stability in Human Urine, Plasma, and Serum: A Review
gold_documents.author: Stevens et al.

examples.question: What happened to the EDTA-plasma metabolome when blood was exposed to room temperature before processing?
gold_answers: significant changes of 64 features in the EDTA-plasma metabolome were detected when blood was exposed to room temperature for 2, 4, 8, and 24 h.

gold_documents.title: Preanalytical aspects and sample quality assessment in metabolomics studies of human blood
gold_documents.author: Yin et al.

examples.question: Which pre-analytical variations produced significant metabolite changes in human plasma profiling?
gold_answers: Short-term storage of blood, hemolysis, and short-term storage of noncooled plasma resulted in statistically significant increases of 4% to 19%

gold_documents.title: Quality markers addressing preanalytical variations of blood and plasma processing identified by broad and targeted metabolite profiling
gold_documents.author: Kamlage et al.

examples.question: Which pre-analytical steps may affect metabolic profiles of blood samples in metabolomics studies?
gold_answers: Collection tubes, hemolysis, delay at room temperature, and freeze-thaw cycles may affect metabolic profiles of blood samples.

gold_documents.title: The key points in the pre-analytical procedures of blood and urine samples in metabolomics studies
gold_documents.author: Bi et al.

examples.question: How did four freeze-thaw cycles affect circulating miRNA concentrations in plasma and serum?
gold_answers: Repetitive (n = 4) freeze-thaw cycles resulted in a significant reduction of miRNA concentration both in plasma and serum samples.

gold_documents.title: Stability of Circulating Blood-Based MicroRNAs – Pre-Analytic Methodological Considerations
gold_documents.author: Glinge et al.

examples.question: How did five freeze-thaw cycles affect MMP-7 and VEGF biomarker levels?
gold_answers: MMP-7 and VEGF levels increased up to >15% after five freeze–thaw cycles and showed a tendency to increase with the number of freeze–thaw cycles.

gold_documents.title: Effect of Repeated Freezing and Thawing on Biomarker Stability in Plasma and Serum Samples
gold_documents.author: Lee et al.

examples.question: How stable were cytokines, chemokines and soluble activation markers in unprocessed EDTA blood stored refrigerated for 24 hours?
gold_answers: All the biomarkers studied, with the exception of IL-1ra, were stable in unprocessed EDTA blood stored at refrigerator temperature for 24h.

gold_documents.title: Stability of cytokines, chemokines and soluble activation markers in unprocessed blood stored under different conditions
gold_documents.author: Aziz et al.

examples.question: Were inflammatory marker concentrations affected more in serum or plasma after delayed whole-blood storage?
gold_answers: The concentrations in serum generally increased more than in plasma. The measurable concentrations of inflammatory markers also changed in DBSS stored under various conditions.

gold_documents.title: Effects of blood sample handling procedures on measurable inflammatory markers in plasma, serum and dried blood spot samples
gold_documents.author: Skogstrand et al.

examples.question: Do storage conditions affect the stability of small-molecule metabolites in cerebrospinal fluid?
gold_answers: small-molecule metabolites in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are relatively unaffected by 1–3 freeze/thaw cycles, by storage at −20 °C up to two months.

gold_documents.title: Assessing the Pre-Analytical Stability of Small-Molecule Metabolites in Cerebrospinal Fluid Using Direct-Infusion Metabolomics
gold_documents.author: Haijes et al.

examples.question: Why is stabilization important for fluid biospecimens kept at room temperature?
gold_answers: Specimen stabilization is imperative, because fluid biospecimens degrade quickly when kept untreated at room temperature.

gold_documents.title: State of the art in preservation of fluid biospecimens
gold_documents.author: Hubel et al.

examples.question: Which cytokine remained stable when whole-blood centrifugation was delayed at room temperature for 48 hours?
gold_answers: IL-17A was stable in both plasma and serum samples, even when whole-blood centrifugation was delayed at room temperature for 48 h.

gold_documents.title: Impact of Whole-Blood Processing Conditions on Plasma and Serum Concentrations of Cytokines
gold_documents.author: Lee et al.

examples.question: What happens to serum potassium when serum is refrigerated in collection tubes containing separating gel?
gold_answers: Potassium levels increase when serum is refrigerated in collection tubes containing separating gel. This can be attributed to contamination of the serum layer.

gold_documents.title: Increase in Serum Potassium Levels After Refrigerated Storage: A Component of Blood Clot Contaminates the Serum Layer Over the Separator Gel
gold_documents.author: Yoshida et al.

examples.question: Which specimen type preserved potassium and creatinine better than serum or plasma tubes?
gold_answers: Potassium and creatinine were more stable in gel tubes than in serum/plasma tubes. In contrast, phentytoin was stable in plain serum and plasma.

gold_documents.title: Evaluation of three different specimen types (serum, plasma lithium heparin and serum gel separator) for analysis of certain analytes: clinical significance of differences in results and efficiency in use
gold_documents.author: O'Keane and Cunningham
